title: Start small then grow
summary: A responsive prefix applies a class from a chosen screen width upwards.
introduction: A responsive prefix applies a class from a chosen screen width upwards. Your task: Resize the page and find where the second column appears.

Explain the example for start small then grow

blocks.text: A responsive prefix applies a class from a chosen screen width upwards. Unprefixed classes are the starting rules for all widths.

These examples use Tailwind CSS 4 in a separate project. Install tailwindcss and @tailwindcss/cli. Put @import "tailwindcss"; in input.css and build with npx @tailwindcss/cli -i input.css -o output.css. Link output.css in HTML.

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `p-4` adds inner space using Tailwind's spacing scale. It is a scale step rather than four pixels.
`grid-cols-2` defines two grid columns. The `grid` class is also needed to make a grid layout.
The `md:` prefix starts that two-column rule from the medium breakpoint upward. Unprefixed classes describe the base layout.

blocks.text: The books stack at small widths. At the default md breakpoint and above, they form two columns.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: md means a minimum width here. It does not mean only one exact device or screen size.
